query: How can Singapore Airlines improve its overall rating and recommendation rate, especially on flights where passengers do not recommend it (Recommended = no)?

per_column.name: crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: A candidate cause of overall rating and recommendation, capturing perceived attentiveness/warmth of crew as an experiential driver whose effect on the outcome can be attributed.

per_column.name: food_quality_issue_type
per_column.rationale: Another candidate cause (food service failures) that plausibly drives dissatisfaction and non-recommendation; an experiential driver of the outcome rather than a common cause of another treatment.

per_column.name: amenity_reduction_signal
per_column.rationale: Cost-cutting / amenity reduction plausibly affects both service quality delivered (treatment) and passenger ratings (outcome), acting as a common cause; surfaced from review text, not in query.

per_column.name: cabin_class_value_gap
per_column.rationale: The gap between expected and delivered value by class relates to expectations and product tier, which can influence both perceived service and the overall rating; not simply on the crew->rating path. Borderline, but plausibly a common cause of expectation-driven service perception and outcome.

per_column.name: perceived_service_decline
per_column.rationale: A perception of service decline sits on the causal path between actual service quality (treatment) and the rating/recommendation (outcome); it is an intermediate perception, not a common cause, so treating it as a confounder would be an error.

judge.rationale: The added columns clearly supply treatments (crew_service_quality, food_quality_issue_type) that are candidate causes of the outcome, none copied from the query. However, the confounder story is weak. amenity_reduction_signal and cabin_class_value_gap are the only plausible common causes, and even these read more as alternative treatments/expectation moderators than as clean common causes of a specific treatment AND the outcome. perceived_service_decline is a mediator (on the treatment->outcome path) and must not be adjusted for. Overall the set demonstrates driver decomposition more than a properly specified causal-adjustment design: treatments are present, but genuine surfaced confounders are thin and partly ambiguous, so confounder quality is low.
